question: Xi Jinping out before 2027?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if China's General Secretary of the Communist Party, Xi Jinping, is removed from power for any length of time between July 3, 2025, and December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

CCP General Secretary Xi Jinping will be considered removed from power if he announces his resignation from his role as General Secretary, or is otherwise dismissed, detained, disqualified, or otherwise loses his position or is prevented from fulfilling his duties as General Secretary within this market's timeframe.

The primary resolution source for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting.

eventMetadata.context_description: Xi Jinping’s entrenched authority within the Chinese Communist Party and People’s Liberation Army underpins the 95.5% trader consensus against his removal before 2027. Recent military purges, including the January 2026 sidelining of senior generals, have eliminated potential rivals and reinforced loyalty rather than signaling weakness, while preparations for the 21st Party Congress point toward expectations of a fourth term. No major leadership challenges or health developments have surfaced in the past several months to shift this assessment. The wisdom of crowds reflected in current pricing accounts for the opacity of elite politics and historical patterns of incumbent consolidation in one-party systems. Sudden health events, severe economic shocks prompting elite realignment, or unforeseen external crises remain low-probability factors that could still alter outcomes within the resolution window.

eventMetadata.context_description: AOC leads the 2028 Democratic presidential nomination market at 20.9 percent, narrowly ahead of Newsom at 17.3 percent and Ossoff at 14.8 percent, reflecting a fragmented field with no dominant candidate two years after the prior cycle. Trader positioning tracks AOC’s elevated profile among progressive voters and recent primary successes, alongside her fundraising and national visibility through candidate endorsements. Newsom’s earlier market share has eased amid questions over California governance and general-election appeal, while Ossoff benefits from Senate reelection momentum in Georgia and perceptions of broader electability. Polls remain fluid, with Buttigieg, Harris, and Shapiro also drawing measurable support in early surveys. The DNC’s finalized primary calendar—South Carolina first, followed by Nevada, New Hampshire, New Mexico, Michigan, and Virginia—adds scheduling uncertainty that could reward candidates strong in diverse early states. Midterm Senate results and any exploratory announcements before 2027 will likely widen or narrow gaps among these contenders.
